correctness.rationale: Reconstructed universal sufficiency: equality of magnitudes on |z|=1 cancels the top Fourier coefficient in the difference on |z|=r, leaving a real trigonometric polynomial degree <=d−1. Equality at any 2d−1 distinct inner samples makes that difference identically zero. Reflection identities for the rational quotient f/g on the two circles imply R(r²z)=R(z), so rational Laurent coefficients force constant unimodular R. Sharpness: for d>=3 and any 0<r<1 choose A²=(1-r^{2d})/(r²-r^{2d−2})>0, f=1+A z^{d−1}, g=A z+z^d: identical entire outer magnitudes, inner squared-modulus difference 2A r^{d−1}(1-r²)cos((d−1)t) with exactly 2d−2 zeros. d=2 separate f=1+i c z+z² and g=1−i c z+z² give -4 c r(1-r²)sin t, d=1 reciprocal pair shows zero samples insufficient. Independently evaluated all 2d−2 zeros at r=1/2 for d=3,4,5: maximum squared-intensity residual <9e-16. Finite checks are illustrative of the exact identities.
